getCommand.symbolBoundary: local code inside master(action*); not an independently exported symbol
getCommand.behavior: scan BattleCmd for B<opcode>| at a command boundary; B must be preceded by '|' or be at the command start; return the opcode byte; return -1 on NUL before a match

BattleCmd.transfer: copy selected BattleCmdBak slot into BattleCmd, then advance read pointer
BattleCmd.separation: separate from the BattleStatus receive ring used by lssproto_B_recv() C branch

numeric.encoding: uppercase hexadecimal nibbles, accumulated by shift-left 4 and add
numeric.delimiter: after a number begins, first non-hex byte ends the token; the cursor remains at the delimiter for caller-specific handling
numeric.emptyAtNul: returns -1 when no digit is present and input is at NUL
numeric.safetyBoundary: native parser has no explicit token-length bound in the observed routine; a reconstruction parser must impose safe input and range checks

text.boundary: legacy multibyte byte-copy logic; not a general UTF-8 decoder; no per-buffer bound check observed

commandDispatch.note: Opcode byte is returned by local get_command() from a B<opcode>| token. Meanings are recorded only to the extent directly visible in target behavior or explicitly marked as cross-source.

observed.targetBehavior: build/display battle text window; parse up to four TAB-separated strings through get_command_asc(); play sound 202
conditional battle-effect branch is present in target; effect-specific detail depends on the compiled feature path
battle-model path initializes participant/action visual state and creates/updates attack actions
for the target-index-outside-party path, parse and write the battle variable to master action attribute state
malfunction/status-result path updates participant state and can create/remove status actions
damage/result application branch; ATT_DAMAGE name is cross-source semantic corroboration

targetBehavior.selectedParticipant: target index resolves through p_party[] to a participant ACTION
targetBehavior.values: the client consumes server-supplied result category, subtype and numeric amounts; the examined consumer does not calculate authoritative damage
optionalTokens: p: pet damage follows the player damage value
m: optional MP adjustment token in the relevant recovery branch
targetBehavior.repeat: after applying one result, the target probes the next command; if it is another D and its result category/subtype match the current group, it loops to process the next participant; otherwise it restores the command cursor and leaves the next command for the outer state machine

category3.observed: conditional special branch exists in public semantic source under _PETSKILL_LER; target feature identity is not asserted from the source alone

crossSourceReference.role: semantic reference only; exact source/build identity with the audited APK is not established

directUse: preserve separate BattleCmd and BattleStatus receive paths
parse B<opcode>| records with bounded token readers
treat D values as authoritative client-side result inputs rather than recomputing damage from the command consumer
apply only the target-confirmed HP/MP/pet state changes and animation/effect transitions

some optional result branches remain build-feature-dependent and must not be blindly enabled

creation.behavior: allocates a display ACTION via GetAction(0x4a,0x264); when allocation succeeds, installs the damage-number callback, sets display priority and source-relative position, and copies the source damage/pet-damage/MP/recovery flags into the new action

specialVisualBranch.condition: second argument/type equals 3 and source ACTION graphic at +0x180 equals one of 0x18db7 (101815), 0x1d532 (120114), or 0x19650 (104016)
specialVisualBranch.effectAction: GetAction(0x47,0x264); if allocation succeeds, stores the source ACTION in the new effect work field at +0x04 and links the effect ACTION through source work+0x110
specialVisualBranch.boundary: The branch and numeric values are target-observed; the visible effect's gameplay meaning is not inferred from graphic IDs alone.

lifetime.behavior: target exports a separate per-frame display callback for the damage-number ACTION; the full rendering/decay state machine is not yet exhaustively translated into the contract

damageNumberVisual.boundary: damage-number ACTION is a presentation child; it does not itself establish server-side hit or damage calculation

dispatch.behavior: compares an ACTION function/name field against the damage-number callback pointer and dispatches matching ACTIONs to showDamage_num(action*) for display

actionFields.0x170: Per-callback integer counter modified by the visible state machine; semantic struct name unresolved
actionFields.0x174: Set to 16 at state 0 -> 1; no further direct write observed in showDamage_num

lifecycle.initialization: set_damage_num() initializes action+0x170 to 0x18 (24) and action+0xe0 to 2; the work state is obtained from GetAction allocation.
lifecycle.transitionGate: State advancement is skipped when both the first observed global gate is nonzero and the low two bits of the second observed global word are nonzero. The meanings of these globals are unresolved; rendering paths remain reachable.

states.transition: When action+0x170 becomes 0, set action+0x174=16 and work[0]=1.
When action+0x170 reaches or exceeds 24, set work[1]=60 and work[0]=2.

states.perCallback: set action+0x170=0 and decrement work[1] as a byte
states.transition: When the decremented work[1] is 0, clear the related source action's +0xd10 field and call DeathAction() for the damage-number ACTION.

lifecycle.normalFrameTail: After a non-expiry rendering path, call pattern(action,0,1). The expiry path calls DeathAction() and exits without reaching this normal tail.
lifecycle.verification: The state-byte tests, counter steps (2), threshold (24), timer value (60), source cleanup field (+0xd10), and DeathAction() termination are directly visible in the target x86 instructions and corroborated by the ARMv7a Thumb instructions.

rendering.selector: The work field at +0x130 selects target formatting/result-display branches; the callback builds one or more text buffers before dispatching to the damage-font renderer.
rendering.formattingBuffers: The inspected path clears and writes fixed 0x100-byte stack buffers with sprintf; no explicit output-length guard was observed at these sites.
rendering.primaryRenderer: stockFontNumToDamage() receives font number 101 (0x65). Depending on the selected branch it uses a fixed battle-font mode or the mode held at work+0x1ec; getFontNumWidthToDamage() is used in the centered-text paths.

secondaryRenderer.work+0x238: When nonzero, an additional text buffer is submitted with battle-font mode 2 at action.y+12.
secondaryRenderer.work+0x234: When equal to 1, an additional text buffer is measured and submitted at action.y+60.

rendering.alternatePrimaryPath: When work+0x244 equals 1, the primary text uses the alternate fixed-mode-3 path; otherwise the width-measured path is used.
rendering.auxiliaryDisplay: When the related source action's +0xd10 field equals 2, the callback submits an additional StockDispBuffer callback at action.x+2, action.y-22. Its visual meaning is not assigned beyond the observed coordinates and condition.
rendering.boundary: The callback's branch-specific strings, glyph rendering implementation and all special display combinations are not fully translated; the evidence records only the directly observed dispatch and positioning rules.

NextCharLength.classification: leading-byte classifier; no continuation-byte validation observed

getBmpNoFromFont.behavior: uses FindLua() to obtain a Lua state, retrieves the font mapping field, requires it to be a function, calls it with the character byte string and fontBattleType, and returns the numeric result truncated to int; missing state/function, pcall failure or nonnumeric result returns -1
getBmpNoFromFont.boundary: Lua function/asset mapping is runtime data and is not reconstructed from the APK binary alone

getFontNumWidthToDamage.behavior: walks input using NextCharLength; for lengths 1 or 3, copies that byte sequence into a temporary NUL-terminated buffer, maps it through getBmpNoFromFont, and adds the signed 16-bit glyph width from getRealWidthFromMapNo when mapping is nonnegative; advances the input by the reported byte length
getFontNumWidthToDamage.unhandledLengths: 2, 4, 5 and 6 byte units advance the input but contribute no width; length 0 ends the scan
getFontNumWidthToDamage.boundary: native temporary buffer has no observed explicit bound check; reconstruction must use bounded input and glyph strings

stockFontNumToDamage.perCharacterFlow: for each 1-byte or 3-byte unit, copies bytes to a temporary NUL-terminated string, calls getBmpNoFromFont, and when the result is nonnegative submits one glyph to the display queue; then gets the glyph width and advances the x cursor by that signed 16-bit width
stockFontNumToDamage.queueSelection: effective bool argument bit 0 selects StockFixedDispBuffer when set, otherwise StockDispBuffer; a separate observed global byte bit 0 forces the effective bool to 1
stockFontNumToDamage.unhandledLengths: 2, 4, 5 and 6 byte units advance the input but do not submit a glyph; length 0 stops rendering
stockFontNumToDamage.fontWidth: uses getRealWidthFromMapNo(bitmapNo, &width, &height); cursor advance uses the returned signed 16-bit width
stockFontNumToDamage.boundary: fixed-size temporary buffers and legacy byte-length handling; no general UTF-8 guarantees or explicit text-length bound observed
